tools.name: list_propositions
tools.description: List every service, with the business it belongs to and a one-line summary: lookups that run instantly, and requirements you can send.

tools.name: describe_proposition
tools.description: Everything about one service, by the slug list_propositions gives: what happens to a request, what you receive, scope and limits, the request fields with examples, and the lookups it runs.

tools.name: submit_request
tools.description: Send a requirement to any service, or describe one none of them lists (slug "anything-else"). It is recorded and answered with a receipt: keep its id and token to read the request's status (request_status), to add details later (continuation), and to act on an offer made in reply. A requirement is n

tools.name: screen_sanctions
tools.description: Plumbline: Screen a person or company name against the US Treasury OFAC SDN list and its aliases (US OFAC SDN only: not the EU, UK or UN lists). Returns each match with its score, SDN entry number, type and programs, and the date the list was published. A match is a lead for review, not a determinat

tools.name: company_financial_facts
tools.description: Plumbline: Reported values of one XBRL concept for one SEC filer, by CIK or ticker, from its SEC filings (EDGAR): each value with its period, fiscal year, form, filing date and accession number, the latest 40.

tools.name: federal_contract_awards
tools.description: Plumbline: US federal contract actions (awards and modifications) by vendor name, NAICS code, place-of-performance state and fiscal year, ten at a time, from FPDS, the government's contract reporting system.

tools.name: extract_web_page
tools.description: Decant: Read one public web page into title, headings, text, links and JSON-LD. robots.txt is honoured.

tools.name: convert_document
tools.description: Decant: Convert an uploaded file (file_base64) or public URL: CSV and XLSX become JSON rows per sheet; text PDFs become text per page. Up to 5 MB decoded, 20,000 rows per sheet; no OCR, PDF table grids or schema extraction. No account or API key; free within the shared daily limit. Files are sent to

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: screen_sanctions, extract_web_page · Private data: submit_request, convert_document · Public sink: list_propositions, submit_request, convert_document · Destructive: list_propositions.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: screen_sanctions, extract_web_page · Private data: submit_request, convert_document · Public sink: list_propositions, submit_request, convert_document · Destructive: list_propositions

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "describe_proposition" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Everything about one service: what happens to a request, what you get, scope and limits, the request fields and any operations." → after: "Everything about one service, by the slug list_propositions gives: what happens to a request, what you receive, scope and limits, the request fields with examples, and the lookups it runs."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
